positions.name: Goalkeeper
positions.blurb: Owns the box. Needs reach, a fast standing jump and sharp reactions more than running volume.

positions.name: Centre-back
positions.blurb: Wins the ball in the air and holds the line. Height and jump dominate, with enough pace to cover.

positions.name: Full-back
positions.blurb: Up and down the touchline for 90 minutes. Endurance plus repeatable sprint speed.

positions.name: Central Midfielder
positions.blurb: Covers the most ground on the pitch. Aerobic capacity first, everything else second.

positions.name: Winger
positions.blurb: Beats a defender one-on-one. Top-end speed and change of direction are the whole job.

positions.name: Striker
positions.blurb: Finishes chances. Explosive over 5-30m, strong in the air, doesn't need midfield lungs.

positions.name: Point Guard
positions.blurb: Brings the ball up and creates. Lateral quickness and first-step speed outweigh size.

positions.name: Shooting Guard
positions.blurb: Scores off movement. Needs elevation to shoot over closeouts plus guard-level agility.

positions.name: Small Forward
positions.blurb: The all-rounder. Balanced size, reach and explosiveness - no single dominant trait.

positions.name: Power Forward
positions.blurb: Works in traffic. Standing jump and frame matter more than run-up leaping.

positions.name: Centre
positions.blurb: Protects the rim and rebounds. Standing reach is the single biggest predictor here.

positions.name: Setter
positions.blurb: Touches the second ball every rally. Footwork and court coverage come before power.

positions.name: Libero
positions.blurb: Back-court defence specialist. Pure reaction and agility - height is close to irrelevant.

positions.name: Outside Hitter
positions.blurb: Main attacking option. Spike reach and arm speed carry the position.

positions.name: Middle Blocker
positions.blurb: Lives at the net. Block touch and standing reach decide how much of the net gets covered.

positions.name: Opposite / Server
positions.blurb: Points from the service line and the right side. Raw arm velocity is the differentiator.

positions.name: Opening Batsman
positions.blurb: Faces the new ball and turns ones into twos. Short-sprint speed above all.

positions.name: Middle-order Batsman
positions.blurb: Bats long and runs hard in the middle overs. Endurance-weighted profile.

positions.name: Fast Bowler
positions.blurb: Bowls long spells at pace. Speed plus the aerobic base to repeat it.

positions.name: Spin Bowler
positions.blurb: Bowls into the wind all day. Stamina and fielding mobility, not raw pace.

positions.name: Wicketkeeper
positions.blurb: Up and down behind the stumps for the full innings. Quick feet, high work rate.

positions.name: All-rounder
positions.blurb: Does two jobs in one match. Needs a flat, high profile with no weak link.

positions.name: Attacking / Power player
positions.blurb: Ends rallies early with smashes and flat drives. Jump height and grip strength lead.

positions.name: Defensive / Counter player
positions.blurb: Wins by retrieving everything. Court coverage and aerobic capacity are the weapons.

positions.name: All-court / Balanced
positions.blurb: Switches styles mid-match. Wants an even spread with no obvious hole.

positions.name: Attacking / Power player
positions.blurb: Ends rallies early with smashes and flat drives. Jump height and grip strength lead.

positions.name: Defensive / Counter player
positions.blurb: Wins by retrieving everything. Court coverage and aerobic capacity are the weapons.

positions.name: All-court / Balanced
positions.blurb: Switches styles mid-match. Wants an even spread with no obvious hole.

positions.name: Chaser
positions.blurb: Pole dives, direction changes and the sitting-to-sprint transition. Flexibility matters here.

positions.name: Runner / Dodger
positions.blurb: Survives as long as possible in the square. Straight-line speed plus evasive footwork.
